_about: Animation overhaul, unit D (docs/animation/overhaul-plan.md): what the ragdoll does beyond its springs. shapes: each fighter's tuck, brace, skid and crumple targets, one angle (rad) per degree of freedom of ragdoll.json in its order, converted from Art's silhouette reference (art/concepts/silhouettes/gen.mjs; P circles, A blades, E wedges, C steps); fighters maps a roster id to a shape key (a placeholder map until the four fighters have theirs). flail: the early-launch limb flail (amp in rad and hz per degree of freedom, and the stateT window over which it fades out). regimes: tuck_max the most a tumble tucks, tuck_spin the spin (rad/s) over which it tucks, tuck_after the stateT window before which it does not, skid_w and crumple_down_w the weight of the skid and crumple shapes. hit: the hit-reaction kicks: for each degree of freedom and each region hit (head, core, arms, legs) the kick in rad/s is gain x force x (kx x dx x (1 + vx x v) + ky x dy + kc x w), dx and dy the blow's push in the body frame (x forward), v and w the deterministic variants of the hit in -1 to 1 (vx_var and kc_var name them: u, u2, or one for a constant 1). Render only, outside the sim's data hash.

weight._note: RG1 (docs/animation/ragdoll-physics-paper.md): mass divides every impulse and the flail (a heavier body moves less per blow); tier_gain multiplies them by the power tier of the opponent, 1 to 4 (a bigger blow sends the limbs further); the lag per degree of freedom is in ragdoll.json (head 0 ticks, trunk 2, arms 4 to 5, legs 5 to 6). First values, Animation own; the masses are placeholders until Game Design gives the fighters a mass.
